intro.title: Build branded types for IDs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user management system that uses TypeScript's branded types to create distinct, type-safe identifiers for different entities, like User IDs and Product IDs. You'll learn how branded types prevent mixing up different kinds of IDs at compile time, enhancing code safety. The core concepts involve using intersection types with a unique brand property to create these distinct types. You'll implement this by defining branded type aliases and using them in functions to ensure only the correct ID type is accepted.
intro.usecase: Branded types for IDs are essential in enterprise applications where multiple types of IDs must be distinguished at compile time. In e-commerce dashboards, you might have ProductID, OrderID, and UserID values that all look like strings but represent fundamentally different entities. TypeScript's structural typing would normally allow these to be mixed accidentally, but branded types prevent shipping an order with a user ID or displaying product details for an order ID. This pattern is commonly used in financial systems, inventory management interfaces, and customer relationship platforms where data integrity is critical.
